entity_title: First 3 months: no residence document required
fact_text: For the first three months an EU/EEA national needs no residence document to live in Lithuania - the right of residence is automatic. Lithuania cannot require you to apply for a residence document in this period, though you may have to report your presence on arrival.
evidence_quote: During the first 3 months of your stay in your new country, as EU national, you cannot be required to apply for a residence document confirming your right to live there - although in some countries you may have to report your presence upon arrival.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR often assumes an EU hire must obtain a permit before starting; for the first 3 months there is no residence document to obtain at all.

fact_text: An EU/EEA national staying in Lithuania longer than three months may be required to register their residence with the relevant authority and be issued a registration certificate.
evidence_quote: After 3 months in your new country, you may be required to register your residence with the relevant authority (often the town hall or local police station), and to be issued with a registration certificate.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The registration trigger is the 3-month mark, not the arrival date - the obligation appears only after 90 days of residence.

entity_title: EU citizens get a certificate, not a permit
fact_text: EU/EEA nationals are not issued a residence permit but a registration certificate that merely confirms an already-existing right of residence; the right exists in law before any document.
evidence_quote: This certificate confirms your right to live in your new country.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The certificate is declaratory, not constitutive - unlike a third-country residence permit it records a right the person already holds under free movement.

entity_title: Non-registration is a fine, not expulsion
fact_text: If registration is required and the EU/EEA national fails to register, they may be fined, but they keep the right to live in Lithuania and cannot be expelled solely for not registering.
evidence_quote: If you are required to register, you may be fined for not doing so but may continue to live in the country and cannot be expelled just for this.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A missed registration is a fineable administrative matter, not a loss of residence right - a common HR misconception.

entity_title: You can start work before the certificate is issued
fact_text: An EU/EEA national's right to take up work is not gated by the registration certificate; the cited example is self-employment, and the authorities must in any case issue the certificate immediately when asked.
evidence_quote: as an EU national, Kurt may work as a self-employed person without waiting for a registration certificate.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR sometimes withholds a start date pending the certificate; the free-movement right to work does not wait for the paperwork.

entity_title: Tax residency at 183 days in the year
fact_text: A person present in Lithuania for 183 days or more during the tax period (calendar year) is a Lithuanian tax resident, taxable on worldwide income - separate from immigration residence status.
evidence_quote: any natural person who is present in Lithuania continuously or intermittently for 183 days or more during the tax period

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Tax residency is set by day-count under the Law on Personal Income Tax, independent of the EU residence certificate; an assignee can be a tax resident without having registered residence.

fact_text: Even if under 183 days in a single year, an individual becomes a Lithuanian tax resident if present 280 days or more across two successive tax periods, provided at least 90 of those days fall in one of the years.
evidence_quote: any natural person who is present in Lithuania continuously or intermittently for 280 days or more during successive tax periods and stayed in Lithuania continuously or intermittently for 90 days or more during one of those tax periods

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Baltic-specific trap: staying just under 183 days each year can still make you a Lithuanian tax resident via the two-year 280-day rolling count.

entity_title: Centre of interests can trigger residency alone
fact_text: Independently of any day-count, a person whose centre of personal, social or economic interests is in Lithuania rather than abroad during the tax period is a Lithuanian tax resident.
evidence_quote: any natural person whose place of personal, social or economic interests during the tax period is in Lithuania rather than in a foreign country

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Relocating family and main economic ties to Lithuania can establish tax residency before any day threshold is reached.

entity_title: PSD cover is automatic only via employment
fact_text: State healthcare depends on compulsory health insurance (PSD). For an employee the health-insurance contribution is withheld from pay automatically, so cover follows the employment contract.
evidence_quote: Compulsory health insurance payments under the terms of a contract of employment or a copyright agreement are deducted automatically.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: PSD cover for an employed EU hire is automatic through payroll, but it hinges on the contract/contribution existing - residence alone does not insure you.

entity_title: PSD gap: buy it privately if not in an insured group
fact_text: An EU/EEA national who is not employed, self-employed, nor on the state-insured list is not covered by PSD and must purchase compulsory health insurance privately to be insured.
evidence_quote: you must acquire compulsory health insurance privately

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Gap trap: between arrival and first payroll, or for a non-working accompanying spouse, there is no automatic PSD cover - it must be paid personally.

entity_title: Uninsured pay full cost; only emergencies are universal
fact_text: Everyone in Lithuania can receive emergency medical assistance, but a person who has not paid compulsory health insurance contributions must pay the full cost of any other treatment themselves.
evidence_quote: Those who have not paid compulsory health contributions (or have not had them paid on their behalf) must cover the cost of their treatment.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Emergency care is universal, but routine and specialist care is billed to the uninsured - the PSD gap has direct financial exposure.

fact_text: Whether a person has the right to compulsory health insurance in Lithuania depends on whether they are listed in the population register, so entry in the register is an administrative precondition for health cover, not merely paying contributions.
evidence_quote: In deciding whether a person has the right to compulsory health insurance, account must be taken of whether or not they are listed in the population register.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The population-register entry (which is where the Lithuanian personal code is assigned) is the master key: without it, even paid contributions may not translate into recognised PSD cover.

entity_title: Only the health contribution is compulsory for all
fact_text: Most Lithuanian social security benefits depend on a person's activity and past insurance contributions; of the Sodra contributions, only the health insurance contribution is compulsory.
evidence_quote: Only health insurance contributions are compulsory.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Sodra covers pensions, sickness and more on a contributory basis, but the element compulsory for everyone is the health (PSD) contribution.

entity_title: Working EU citizens skip the 3-month benefit wait
fact_text: EU/EEA citizens and their family members with a right of residence can claim Lithuanian family/child benefits; family members normally need three months' residence, but that waiting requirement does not apply where the EU/EEA citizen or family member works in Lithuania.
evidence_quote: This requirement does not apply if you or a member of your family are citizens of one of the countries mentioned above and work in Lithuania;

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Employment unlocks child benefits immediately for an EU/EEA hire; the 3-month residence wait bites only on non-working family members.

entity_title: EHIC is issued only on the insured person's request
fact_text: For a person insured under PSD in Lithuania, the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) is issued by the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) or its municipal representatives, and only at the insured person's request.
evidence_quote: The card is issued and changed only at the request of the insured person.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The EHIC is not automatic on becoming insured - the insured person must apply for it, e.g. before travelling back to the home country.
